label: model_selection_iter1
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 1: replace the linear baseline with a gradient-boosted tree ensemble (hist_gbdt) fitted on all 2,760 training rows, no early stopping, no scaling needed. Spambase's signal is in threshold-like interactions of highly skewed frequency counts, which is exactly where a boosted tree ranking beats a scaled logistic ranking; the goal explicitly requires moving the ranking (KS 0.8466 -> ~0.934), not the cut. Configuration: 400 boosting iterations at learning_rate 0.06, max_leaf_nodes 31, l2_regularization 1.0, early_stopping off so every training row is used. Class balance is mild (1.54:1) and the baseline's recall<path> are already close, so leave class_weight at default this attempt and read cut_headroom, roc_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut to see how much of any remaining gap is ranking versus operating point before spending an attempt on the imbalance lever.",
  "model_family": "gbdt",
  "candidate_models": [
    "hist_gbdt",
    "xgboost",
    "random_forest"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "max_iter": 400,
    "learning_rate": 0.06,
    "max_leaf_nodes": 31,
    "l2_regularization": 1.0,
    "early_stopping": false
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "First attempt of the run: switches family from the card's logreg baseline (linear, standard-scaled) to hist_gbdt, drops standardisation (irrelevant to trees), and fits 400 boosted trees on the full 2,760-row training split with early stopping explicitly disabled.",
  "rationale": "The goal bar 0.967 sits above the baseline's ranking ceiling (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.9233, KS 0.8466), so no threshold or class_weight move on the linear ranking can reach it — the required gain is roughly 0.087 of KS and has to come from a different ranking generator. All 57 columns are numeric, complete, and heavily right-skewed with many exact zeros; a histogram-binned boosted ensemble handles that monotone-but-nonlinear structure and the feature interactions (e.g. capital_run_length_* combined with char_freq_%24<path>) that a single linear boundary cannot express, and spambase is a dataset where GBDT<path> rankings are routinely well above logistic. With 2,760 training rows and 57 features, 400 iterations at lr 0.06 with 31 leaves and l2 1.0 is enough capacity to fit while staying regularised, and cost is far inside the 600 s / 2 GB budget. Early stopping is left off deliberately: 'auto' is inactive at this row count anyway, and asking for it would cost 276 training rows and make the score non-comparable to attempts that keep them. Imbalance is only 1.54:1 and balanced_accuracy needs recall and specificity moved together, so the default cut is the right starting read; train_val_gap plus cut_headroom will tell the next attempt whether to add regularisation, capacity, or a class_weight nudge.",
  "unsupported_claims": [],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 1
}
